newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends mostly down on LME losses.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends mostly down on LME losses.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly down in active trading on Tuesday, following an overnight correction on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most active December 1996 contract ended at 21,060 yuan ($2,535) per tonne, down 130 yuan. It opened at an intra-day high of 21,190 and hit a low of 20,780.
September fell 100 to 21,400 yuan, October 150 to 21,250, November 110 to 21,120, the January 1997 contract 100 to 21,080 and February 120 to 21,090. March rose 30 to 21,040 and April 610 to 20,810.
Combined volume rose sharply to 77,940 tonnes from 40,150.
Copper opened mostly at intra-day highs and fell, before some buying pushing it back later in the session.
Traders said sharp movements on the LME made many Shanghai individuals liquidate their positions.
"Many retail investors were disappointed with sharp movements of the past two days and were afraid to hold positions due to an uncertain short-term market trend," one trader said.
"But all later-maturing contracts still stayed above 21,000-yuan level, which indicated some institutions were optimistic about the trend in the next few days," he added.

Traders said heavy volume showed long and short position holders were mixed about future trends and Shanghai copper is likely to follow the LME trend in the short term due to a lack of market-moving news.
Aluminium ended mostly down. September rose 10 to 14,410 yuan. October fell 90 to 14,390 and November 110 to 14,390.
Combined volume fell to 120 tonnes from 1,710. ($1=8.3058 yuan)
